system: The boundary — what the electrical build hands over
title: The control panel is the DCU's faceplate, not its own board: no DP-KEY, no CAN node, a local ribbon to the DCU behind it
The headlamps are 4x6 rectangular LED units on adapter plates in the retained pop-up buckets
The car's own FB mirrors are kept, and the DCU drives them from a mini thumbstick on the panel with press-to-toggle
The DCU plugs in like the ICU: DT13 flanged receptacles in a printed enclosure wall, the harness on DT06 plug tails
The luxury record is data and is not rendered; pmu_sim/channels.h is hand-synced to electrical pins (F-013)
The radar is a speed-trap radar and laser detector, fully concealed: no unit on the windshield, nothing visible but the warning on the cluster
The tail-light path is chosen after the aperture is measured (V-063)
Parts are chosen in rounds: the agent proposes a product per parts row with why and drawbacks, Camden accepts or vetoes in one block per round, and PICKS.md shows where every part stands
Every parts suggestion is its own block, with the full detail and his answer line right under it; rx7.py picks --ask writes them from the picks table

Parts suggestions live on the project's PICKS.md, laid out like BLOCKS.md: one entry per product with an ANSWER line; he answers any, some or all at leisure, the agent saves his words into picks and only then removes the entry
Parts round 1: eight products accepted - the blower motor, blower final stage, HVAC servos, comfort fuse block, sound deadening, headlamps and both relay sets
Seats first: no add-on heater or cooling kit for now - the search is for front seats with heating and cooling built in, likely with electric controls
